claims.claim: The final and rate-limiting step of Δ7-DA synthesis is catalyzed by DAF-9, a cytochrome P450.
claims.source: The final and rate-limiting step of Δ7-DA synthesis is catalyzed by DAF-9, a cytochrome P450 (Gerisch and Antebi, 2004; Jia et al., 2002; Motola et al., 2006).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Gerisch and Antebi, 2004; Jia et al., 2002; Motola et al., 2006.

claims.claim: In unfavorable environments, Δ7-DA is not produced and unliganded Ce-DAF-12 functions as a transcriptional repressor that arrests growth as L3d larvae in a process known as dauer diapause.
claims.source: In unfavorable environments, Δ7-DA is not produced and unliganded Ce-DAF-12 functions as a transcriptional repressor that arrests growth as L3d larvae in a process known as dauer diapause.
claims.evidence: The claim is directly stated in the manuscript text.

claims.claim: When favorable conditions return, Δ7-DA synthesis resumes, DAF-12 is transcriptionally active, and C. elegans worms exit L3 dauer and continue reproductive development.
claims.source: When favorable conditions return, Δ7-DA synthesis resumes, DAF-12 is transcriptionally active, and worms exit L3 dauer and continue reproductive development.
claims.evidence: The claim is directly stated in the manuscript text.

claims.claim: Pharmacologic administration of Δ7-DA to PP-L1 or PFL-L1 larvae commits them to FL reproductive development, even under conditions that would normally commit them to become L3i.
claims.source: Although the endogenous Ss-DAF-12 ligand was unknown, we demonstrated that pharmacologic administration of Δ7-DA to PP-L1 or PFL-L1 larvae commits them to FL reproductive development, even under conditions that would normally commit them to become L3i (Albarqi et al., 2016; Wang et al., 2009), and institutes a transcriptomic profile in L3i similar to L3+ (Stoltzfus et al., 2014).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Albarqi et al., 2016 and Wang et al., 2009.

claims.claim: Δ7-DA treatment institutes a transcriptomic profile in L3i similar to L3+.
claims.source: Although the endogenous Ss-DAF-12 ligand was unknown, we demonstrated that pharmacologic administration of Δ7-DA to PP-L1 or PFL-L1 larvae commits them to FL reproductive development, even under conditions that would normally commit them to become L3i (Albarqi et al., 2016; Wang et al., 2009), and institutes a transcriptomic profile in L3i similar to L3+ (Stoltzfus et al., 2014).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Stoltzfus et al., 2014.

claims.claim: Knockout of Ss-DAF-12 prevents the formation of L3i larvae.
claims.source: In addition, knockout of Ss-DAF-12 prevents the formation of L3i larvae (Cheong et al., 2021), and in a mouse model of hyperinfection, exogenous Δ7-DA treatment lowers the worm burden in the intestine (Patton et al., 2018).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Cheong et al., 2021.

claims.claim: In a mouse model of hyperinfection, exogenous Δ7-DA treatment lowers the worm burden in the intestine.
claims.source: In addition, knockout of Ss-DAF-12 prevents the formation of L3i larvae (Cheong et al., 2021), and in a mouse model of hyperinfection, exogenous Δ7-DA treatment lowers the worm burden in the intestine (Patton et al., 2018).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Patton et al., 2018.

claims.claim: Δ7-DA was the only ligand activity detected in fraction 23 of HPLC fractionation of S. stercoralis lipids.
claims.source: Among the 70 high-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC) fractions, Ss-DAF-12 ligand activity was detected only in fraction 23 in a cell-based reporter assay and this activity was dose dependent (Figure 2A).
claims.evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 2A.

claims.claim: Fraction 23 coeluted with dafachronic acids.
claims.source: Remarkably, fraction 23 coeluted with dafachronic acids (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B), suggesting that the ligand is a related molecule.
claims.evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1B.

claims.claim: The predicted endogenous concentration of Δ7-DA in S. stercoralis FL-L3 is ~200 nM.
claims.source: The predicted endogenous concentration of Δ7-DA in S. stercoralis FL-L3 is ~200 nM, which is well above the concentration needed to fully activate Ss-DAF-12 (Figure 2B, inset).
claims.evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 2B.

claims.claim: The concentration of Δ7-DA in S. stercoralis FL-L3 (~200 nM) is well above the concentration needed to fully activate Ss-DAF-12.
claims.source: The predicted endogenous concentration of Δ7-DA in S. stercoralis FL-L3 is ~200 nM, which is well above the concentration needed to fully activate Ss-DAF-12 (Figure 2B, inset).
claims.evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 2B inset.

claims.claim: Δ7-DA was present in FL-L1/L2 and was significantly more abundant in the FL-L3 stage as the larvae progress toward reproductive maturity.
claims.source: In the postparasitic environment under conditions that promote FL development, Δ7-DA was present in FL-L1/L2 and was significantly more abundant in the FL-L3 stage as the larvae progress toward reproductive maturity (Figure 3A–C).
claims.evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 3A-C.

claims.claim: Δ7-DA was detected in L3+ that have just infected the host and begun their reproductive development.
claims.source: Similarly, Δ7-DA was detected in L3+ that have just infected the host and begun their reproductive development (Figure 3A–C).
claims.evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 3A-C.

claims.claim: Δ7-DA was undetectable in FL-adults, PFL-L1, and L3i larvae.
claims.source: In concordance with the hypothesis that developmental arrest is due to the absence of a DAF-12 ligand, Δ7-DA was undetectable in FL-adults, PFL-L1, and L3i larvae (Figure 3A–C).
claims.evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 3A-C.

claims.claim: Intestinal (Int)-L1-L3a larvae that were the direct progeny of parasitic adults in hyperinfected gerbils had virtually no Δ7-DA.
claims.source: The intestinal (Int)-L1-L3a larvae that were the direct progeny of parasitic adults in hyperinfected gerbils also had virtually no Δ7-DA (Figure 3A–C).
claims.evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 3A-C.

claims.claim: The highest concentration of Δ7-DA occurred in parasitic adults, as opposed to the essentially undetectable levels in FL adults.
claims.source: Another intriguing finding was that the highest concentration of Δ7-DA occurred in parasitic adults, as opposed to the essentially undetectable levels in FL adults (Figure 3B).
claims.evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 3B.

claims.claim: Parasitic adults live for up to a year or more in the host, whereas FL adults survive for only a few days in soil.
claims.source: This difference in Δ7-DA levels correlated with the markedly different lifespans of the two adult populations. Parasitic adults live for up to a year or more in the host, whereas FL adults survive for only a few days in soil (Lok, 2007; Viney and Lok, 2015).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Lok, 2007 and Viney and Lok, 2015.

claims.claim: Δ7-DA is known to extend lifespan of adult C. elegans.
claims.source: Given that Δ7-DA is known to extend lifespan of adult C. elegans (Gerisch et al., 2007; Yamawaki et al., 2010), this finding suggests that Δ7-DA may play a similar role in extending the lifespan of parasitic adults in S. stercoralis.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Gerisch et al., 2007 and Yamawaki et al., 2010.

claims.claim: Δ7-DA may play a role in extending the lifespan of parasitic adults in S. stercoralis.
claims.source: Given that Δ7-DA is known to extend lifespan of adult C. elegans (Gerisch et al., 2007; Yamawaki et al., 2010), this finding suggests that Δ7-DA may play a similar role in extending the lifespan of parasitic adults in S. stercoralis.
claims.evidence: The claim is speculative, based on inference from C. elegans data.

claims.claim: The S. stercoralis genome contains single homologs for both DAF-36 and DHS-16.
claims.source: Bioinformatic analysis of the S. stercoralis genome revealed single homologs for both DAF-36 and DHS-16 (Stoltzfus et al., 2012), which share sequence identity with their C. elegans counterparts.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Stoltzfus et al., 2012.

claims.claim: There are 26 CYPs in S. stercoralis, but none of these share predictive sequence identity with DAF-9 (~36% at the best).
claims.source: In contrast, there are 26 CYPs in S. stercoralis, but none of these share predictive sequence identity with DAF-9 (~36% at the best) (Stoltzfus et al., 2012).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Stoltzfus et al., 2012.

claims.claim: S. stercoralis synthesizes Δ7-DA from dietary cholesterol in vivo.
claims.source: After 24 hr, we detected significant levels of 13C-labeled Δ7-DA in the FL-L3 (Figure 4B).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4B demonstrating incorporation of 13C-cholesterol into Δ7-DA.

claims.claim: Ss-DAF-36 catalyzes the synthesis of 7-dehydrocholesterol in the first step of Δ7-DA biosynthesis.
claims.source: Sf9 microsomes expressing Ss-DAF-36 readily converted cholesterol to 7-dehydrocholesterol (Figure 4C) with an efficacy comparable to the C. elegans enzyme (Figure 4D).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4C and 4D.

claims.claim: Ss-SCDH-16 catalyzes the conversion of lathosterol to lathosterone in the penultimate step of Δ7-DA biosynthesis.
claims.source: Similarly, Ss-SCDH-16 catalyzed the conversion of lathosterol to lathosterone like Ce-DHS-16 (Figure 4E, F).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4E and 4F.

claims.claim: Ss-CYP22a9 is the DAF-9 isoenzyme in S. stercoralis that synthesizes Δ7-DA from lathosterone.
claims.source: Unambiguously, only one of the 26 CYPs, Ss-CYP22a9 (SSTP_0001032100) synthesized Δ7-DA at levels comparable to Ce-DAF-9 (Figure 4G).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4G demonstrating that only Ss-CYP22a9 among 26 CYPs tested synthesized Δ7-DA.

claims.claim: In the presence of 8-Br-cGMP, endogenous Δ7-DA was increased progressively over a 3-day period to levels (~100 nM) that would saturate Ss-DAF-12 occupancy.
claims.source: In the presence of 8-Br-cGMP, we found that endogenous Δ7-DA was increased progressively over a 3-day period to levels (~100 nM) that would saturate Ss-DAF-12 occupancy (Figure 5).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5.

claims.claim: Stimulation of Δ7-DA synthesis by 8-Br-cGMP correlated exactly with the expression of Ss-cyp22a9.
claims.source: Furthermore, this stimulation of Δ7-DA synthesis correlated exactly with the expression of Ss-cyp22a9 (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A) and was abolished by cotreatment with ketoconazole, a broad-spectrum CYP inhibitor (Figure 5).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1A.

claims.claim: Ketoconazole, a broad-spectrum CYP inhibitor, abolished the stimulation of Δ7-DA synthesis by 8-Br-cGMP.
claims.source: Furthermore, this stimulation of Δ7-DA synthesis correlated exactly with the expression of Ss-cyp22a9 (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A) and was abolished by cotreatment with ketoconazole, a broad-spectrum CYP inhibitor (Figure 5).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5.

claims.claim: Disruption of the Ss-cyp22a9 gene severely impaired cGMP-induced feeding behavior in L3i larvae.
claims.source: In contrast, in Ss-cyp22a9 knockout larvae, cGMP-induced feeding behavior was severely impaired (Figure 5C).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5C.

claims.claim: The loss of feeding behavior in Ss-cyp22a9-deficient larvae was rescued completely by treatment with exogenous Δ7-DA.
claims.source: The loss of this feeding behavior in Ss-cyp22a9-deficient larvae was rescued completely by treatment with exogenous Δ7-DA, further demonstrating the importance of DAF-12 activation as a requirement for parasite development (Figure 5C).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5C.

claims.claim: Disrupting the Ss-cyp22a9 gene abolished the Δ7-DA induction by cGMP.
claims.source: Consistent with the results of the CYP inhibitor, disrupting the Ss-cyp22a9 gene abolished the Δ7-DA induction by cGMP (Figure 5D).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5D.

claims.claim: Δ7-DA treatment for 14 days dramatically reduced fecal larval output by ~90% in gerbils with uncomplicated S. stercoralis infection.
claims.source: Compared to vehicle, treatment with Δ7-DA for 14 days dramatically reduced fecal larval output by ~90% (312 ± 103 larvae per gram feces for vehicle vs 32 ± 6 for DA, q < 0.03; Figure 6).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6.

claims.claim: The numbers of parasitic adults were not significantly changed by Δ7-DA treatment in gerbils with uncomplicated S. stercoralis infection.
claims.source: In contrast, the numbers of parasitic adults, which produce intestinal larvae, were not significantly changed by Δ7-DA treatment (Figure 6B).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6B.

claims.claim: When hyperinfected gerbils were treated with Δ7-DA starting at 10 days after the hyperinfection was initiated, there was a 70% survival rate that lasted for at least 90 days.
claims.source: In contrast, when a matched group of these animals was treated with Δ7-DA starting at 10 days after the hyperinfection was initiated, there was an impressive 70% survival rate that lasted for at least 90 days at which point we arbitrarily terminated the experiment (Figure 7A, blue line).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7A.

claims.claim: Hyperinfection resulted in a massive increase in the number of viable intestinal parasites (>104) in vehicle-treated gerbils, which was reduced substantially in Δ7-DA-treated animals.
claims.source: Autopsies of these animals showed that hyperinfection resulted in a massive increase in the number of viable intestinal parasites (>104) in vehicle-treated gerbils, which was reduced substantially in Δ7-DA-treated animals (Figure 7A-D).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7A-D.

claims.claim: The number of autoinfected L3+ larvae in parenteral tissues was reduced by 90% (and in some cases was undetectable) in Δ7-DA-treated animals compared to vehicle-treated animals.
claims.source: Notably, the number of autoinfected L3+ larvae in parenteral tissues, which drive the resulting pathogenesis, was reduced by 90% (and in some cases was undetectable) in Δ7-DA-treated animals compared to vehicle-treated animals (Figure 7C).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7C.

claims.claim: There was a >10-fold increase in adult parasites in hyperinfected vehicle-treated gerbils compared to vehicle-treated gerbils with uncomplicated infections.
claims.source: Compared to vehicle-treated gerbils with uncomplicated infections (Figure 6B), we observed a >10-fold increase in adult parasites in hyperinfected vehicle-treated gerbils (Figure 7D).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by comparison of experimental data shown in Figure 6B and Figure 7D.

claims.claim: There was a significant decrease in adult parasites in the Δ7-DA-treated gerbils that had a hyperinfection (50% vs. the vehicle treated).
claims.source: However, unlike in the uncomplicated infection, there was a significant decrease in adult parasites in the Δ7-DA-treated gerbils that had a hyperinfection (50% vs. the vehicle treated, Figure 7D).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7D.

claims.claim: Ivermectin treatment at 300 μg/kg delivered i.p. acutely cleared fecal larva output in ~40% of the hyperinfected gerbils within 7 days, resulting in ~25% survival rate for at least 90 days.
claims.source: In this model, 300 μg/kg ivermectin delivered i.p. acutely cleared fecal larva output in ~40% of the hyperinfected gerbils within 7 days, resulting in ~25% survival rate for at least 90 days (Figure 7A, red line).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7A.

claims.claim: Ivermectin was as effective as Δ7-DA in removing adult parasites from animals undergoing hyperinfection.
claims.source: As expected, ivermectin was as effective as Δ7-DA in removing adult parasites from animals undergoing hyperinfection (Figure 7D), but in contrast to Δ7-DA, ivermectin was ineffective at decreasing either the intestinal or L3+ larval populations (Figure 7B, C).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7D.

claims.claim: Ivermectin was ineffective at decreasing either the intestinal or L3+ larval populations in hyperinfected gerbils.
claims.source: As expected, ivermectin was as effective as Δ7-DA in removing adult parasites from animals undergoing hyperinfection (Figure 7D), but in contrast to Δ7-DA, ivermectin was ineffective at decreasing either the intestinal or L3+ larval populations (Figure 7B, C).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7B and 7C.

claims.claim: The combination of Δ7-DA and ivermectin improved the survival rate significantly over either agent alone (>75%) in hyperinfected gerbils.
claims.source: We found that the combination of both agents improved the survival rate significantly over either agent alone (>75%, Figure 7A) and reduced the parasite burden of all life stages (Figure 7B–D).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7A.

claims.claim: The combination of Δ7-DA and ivermectin reduced the parasite burden of all life stages in hyperinfected gerbils.
claims.source: We found that the combination of both agents improved the survival rate significantly over either agent alone (>75%, Figure 7A) and reduced the parasite burden of all life stages (Figure 7B–D).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7B-D.

claims.claim: The combination of Δ7-DA and ivermectin completely eliminated the parasites from all the animals that survived hyperinfection.
claims.source: Remarkably, the combination of Δ7-DA and ivermectin completely eliminated the parasites from all the animals that survived, essentially curing them of the disease (Figure 7E).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7E.

claims.claim: When treated with ivermectin or Δ7-DA alone, ≤10% of surviving animals were parasite-free.
claims.source: In contrast, when treated with ivermectin or Δ7-DA alone, ≤10% were parasite-free even among those animals that survived (Figure 7E).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7E.

claims.claim: Mortality rates in ivermectin-treated patients with hyperinfection range as high as 50%.
claims.source: Mortality rates in ivermectin-treated patients with hyperinfection range as high as 50% (Buonfrate et al., 2013).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Buonfrate et al., 2013.

claims.claim: Ivermectin is highly effective at killing adults and feeding larvae but less effective at killing the developmentally quiescent L3a larvae.
claims.source: As an inhibitor of muscular function, ivermectin is highly effective at killing adults and feeding larvae (Repetto et al., 2018), but less effective at killing the developmentally quiescent L3a larvae that continuously drive autoinfection.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Repetto et al., 2018 and by inference from the mechanism of action.

claims.claim: Δ7-DA directly interferes with infectious L3a larval development by binding to unliganded DAF-12 and provoking an inappropriate developmental response inside the host that results in death of the larvae.
claims.source: In contrast, Δ7-DA directly interferes with infectious L3a larval development by binding to unliganded DAF-12 and provoking an inappropriate developmental response inside the host that results in death of the larvae.
claims.evidence: The claim is based on inference from the experimental data and the known mechanism of DAF-12 activation.

claims.claim: The ligand binding pocket of Ss-DAF-12 is divergent from that of Ce-DAF-12.
claims.source: Indeed, the finding that the ligand binding pocket of Ss-DAF-12 is divergent from that of Ce-DAF-12 (Wang et al., 2009) and the observation that S. stercoralis lacks an obvious ortholog of DAF-9 (the only known DA-synthesizing enzyme found in C. elegans) suggested that the Ss-DAF-12 ligand would likewise be divergent.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Wang et al., 2009.

claims.claim: The Ss-DAF-12 ligand binding domain shares only moderate sequence identity (42%) with its C. elegans homolog.
claims.source: In comparison to its C. elegans homolog, the Ss-DAF-12 ligand binding domain shares only moderate sequence identity (42%) and exhibits a distinct pharmacologic profile in response to Δ7-DA compared to other species (Wang et al., 2009).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Wang et al., 2009.

claims.claim: Ss-DAF-12 exhibits a distinct pharmacologic profile in response to Δ7-DA compared to other species.
claims.source: In comparison to its C. elegans homolog, the Ss-DAF-12 ligand binding domain shares only moderate sequence identity (42%) and exhibits a distinct pharmacologic profile in response to Δ7-DA compared to other species (Wang et al., 2009).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Wang et al., 2009.

claims.claim: The cytochrome P450 (Ss-CYP22a9) that catalyzes the synthesis of Δ7-DA is unique to Strongyloides spp.
claims.source: For example, the cytochrome P450 (Ss-CYP22a9) that catalyzes the synthesis of Δ7-DA (Figure 4) and the ligand-dependent coactivator that Ss-DAF-12 requires for transactivation (Ss-DIP-1) (Cheong et al., 2021) are both unique to Strongyloides spp.
claims.evidence: The claim is directly stated in the manuscript text.

claims.claim: The ligand-dependent coactivator that Ss-DAF-12 requires for transactivation (Ss-DIP-1) is unique to Strongyloides spp.
claims.source: For example, the cytochrome P450 (Ss-CYP22a9) that catalyzes the synthesis of Δ7-DA (Figure 4) and the ligand-dependent coactivator that Ss-DAF-12 requires for transactivation (Ss-DIP-1) (Cheong et al., 2021) are both unique to Strongyloides spp.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Cheong et al., 2021.

claims.claim: No other ligand activities, including other types of dafachronic acids, were detected in S. stercoralis.
claims.source: First, no other ligand activities, including other types of dafachronic acids were detected.
claims.evidence: The claim is based on the experimental data from the ligand purification and detection studies.

claims.claim: Knocking out Ss-cyp22a9 prevents DAF-12-dependent activity in vivo, and that activity is rescued completely by adding back the ligand.
claims.source: Finally, knocking out the daf-9 homolog, Ss-cyp22a9, which is required to synthesize Δ7-DA, prevents DAF-12-dependent activity in vivo, and that activity is rescued completely by adding back the ligand.
claims.evidence: The claim is based on the experimental data shown in Figure 5.

claims.claim: Δ7-DA has been shown to activate DAF-12 homologs in other species.
claims.source: Interestingly, Δ7-DA has been shown to activate DAF-12 homologs in other species (Ayoade et al., 2020; Long et al., 2020; Ma et al., 2019; Ogawa et al., 2009; Wang et al., 2009).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations including Ayoade et al., 2020; Long et al., 2020; Ma et al., 2019; Ogawa et al., 2009; Wang et al., 2009.

claims.claim: Liganded DAF-12 is required at a completely different but essential stage of the lifecycle to promote reproductive growth.
claims.source: However, the observation that liganded DAF-12 also is required at a completely different but essential stage of the lifecycle to promote reproductive growth raises the possibility of also targeting DAF-12 with an antagonist.
claims.evidence: The claim is based on the experimental data showing Δ7-DA levels correlate with reproductive development.

claims.claim: DAF-12 has been found in all nematode species surveyed to date.
claims.source: Given that DAF-12 has been found in all nematode species surveyed to date (Ayoade et al., 2020; Long et al., 2020; Ma et al., 2019; Ogawa et al., 2009; Wang et al., 2009), antagonizing the receptor would be expected to prevent development of adult worms in all parasitic species, offering a unique, broad-spectrum approach for treating most, if not all, nematode parasitisms.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations including Ayoade et al., 2020; Long et al., 2020; Ma et al., 2019; Ogawa et al., 2009; Wang et al., 2009.

claims.claim: Antagonizing DAF-12 would be expected to prevent development of adult worms in all parasitic species.
claims.source: Given that DAF-12 has been found in all nematode species surveyed to date (Ayoade et al., 2020; Long et al., 2020; Ma et al., 2019; Ogawa et al., 2009; Wang et al., 2009), antagonizing the receptor would be expected to prevent development of adult worms in all parasitic species, offering a unique, broad-spectrum approach for treating most, if not all, nematode parasitisms.
claims.evidence: The claim is speculative, based on inference from the conservation of DAF-12 across nematode species.

claims.claim: Ketoconazole was shown previously to block developmental activation of cultured L3i.
claims.source: Indeed, the finding that the broad-spectrum CYP-inhibitor, ketoconazole, was effective at blocking Δ7-DA synthesis in the present study and was shown previously to block developmental activation of cultured L3i (Albarqi et al., 2016) supports this strategy.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Albarqi et al., 2016.

claims.claim: Δ7-DA has a short half-life and relatively poor pharmacokinetic properties in vivo.
claims.source: Typical of most endogenous steroid receptor ligands, Δ7-DA has a short half-life and relatively poor pharmacokinetic properties in vivo (Patton et al., 2018).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Patton et al., 2018.

claims.claim: Pharmacological activation of Ss-DAF-12 overcomes the deficiencies of ivermectin and significantly improves the outcome of strongyloidiasis in a preclinical model of hyperinfection.
claims.source: Our study further revealed the ligand's biosynthetic enzyme as a potential new target that might also be exploited to treat this lethal parasitic disease.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by the experimental data shown in Figure 7.

claims.claim: Pharmacologically activating DAF-12 prevents L3i arrest in the PFL generation.
claims.source: Pharmacologically activating the nuclear receptor DAF-12 has been shown to prevent L3i arrest in the PFL generation (Albarqi et al., 2016; Wang et al., 2009).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Albarqi et al., 2016 and Wang et al., 2009, and is illustrated in Figure 1.

claims.claim: Liganded DAF-12 in S. stercoralis is required for reproductive development.
claims.source: Taken together with our previous work demonstrating that parasites lacking Ss-DAF-12 fail to respond to Δ7-DA and cannot enter or exit the L3i stage (Cheong et al., 2021), we conclude that liganded DAF-12 in S. stercoralis is required for reproductive development, while unliganded DAF-12 is requisite for the production of infectious L3i and L3a larvae.
claims.evidence: The claim is based on inference from the experimental data and previous work cited (Cheong et al., 2021).

claims.claim: Unliganded DAF-12 is requisite for the production of infectious L3i and L3a larvae in S. stercoralis.
claims.source: Taken together with our previous work demonstrating that parasites lacking Ss-DAF-12 fail to respond to Δ7-DA and cannot enter or exit the L3i stage (Cheong et al., 2021), we conclude that liganded DAF-12 in S. stercoralis is required for reproductive development, while unliganded DAF-12 is requisite for the production of infectious L3i and L3a larvae.
claims.evidence: The claim is based on inference from the experimental data and previous work cited (Cheong et al., 2021).

claims.claim: Δ7-DA synthesis is necessary for parasite reproduction in S. stercoralis.
claims.source: Genetic loss of function of the ligand's rate-limiting enzyme demonstrated that Δ7-DA synthesis is necessary for parasite reproduction, whereas its absence is required for the development of infectious larvae.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by the experimental data shown in Figure 5.

claims.claim: The absence of Δ7-DA is required for the development of infectious larvae in S. stercoralis.
claims.source: Genetic loss of function of the ligand's rate-limiting enzyme demonstrated that Δ7-DA synthesis is necessary for parasite reproduction, whereas its absence is required for the development of infectious larvae.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by the experimental data shown in Figure 3.

claims.claim: Availability of the Δ7-DA ligand permits Ss-DAF-12 to function as an on/off switch governing autoinfection.
claims.source: Availability of the ligand permits Ss-DAF-12 to function as an on/off switch governing autoinfection, making it vulnerable to therapeutic intervention.
claims.evidence: The claim is based on inference from the experimental data showing Δ7-DA levels correlate with developmental stages.

claims.claim: In a preclinical model of hyperinfection, pharmacologic activation of DAF-12 suppressed autoinfection and markedly reduced lethality.
claims.source: In a preclinical model of hyperinfection, pharmacologic activation of DAF-12 suppressed autoinfection and markedly reduced lethality.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by the experimental data shown in Figure 7.

claims.claim: When Δ7-DA was administered with ivermectin, the combinatorial effects of the two drugs resulted in a near cure of strongyloidiasis.
claims.source: Moreover, when Δ7-DA was administered with ivermectin, the current but limited drug of choice for treating strongyloidiasis, the combinatorial effects of the two drugs resulted in a near cure of the disease.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by the experimental data shown in Figure 7.

results.result: S. stercoralis is a globally prevalent parasite infecting ~600 million people, with up to 2.5% of infections progressing to hyperinfection syndrome (90% mortality if untreated), often triggered by glucocorticoid administration.
results.evaluation: Claims C1-C4 provide epidemiological context for the disease, all supported by appropriate citations (Buonfrate et al., 2020; Milder et al., 1981). These establish the clinical significance and public health importance of the research.

results.result: The S. stercoralis lifecycle involves complex developmental pathways including environmental and host stages, with unique autoinfection capability allowing persistent infection that can progress to lethal hyperinfection under immunosuppression.
results.evaluation: Claims C5-C19 describe the parasite lifecycle with appropriate citations and are consistent with established knowledge. These provide essential background for understanding the experimental work but represent prior knowledge rather than new findings.

results.result: Current ivermectin treatment has significant limitations, with only 50% efficacy against hyperinfection, inability to eradicate autoinfective larvae, and emerging resistance concerns, particularly relevant given increased glucocorticoid use for SARS-CoV-2.
results.evaluation: Claims C20-C24 establish the clinical need for new therapeutics, all supported by appropriate citations (Krolewiecki et al., 2013; Repetto et al., 2018; Buonfrate et al., 2013; Prichard, 2007; Moloo, 2020). This motivates the study but is not a novel finding.

results.result: In C. elegans, DAF-12 is a conserved nuclear receptor that governs L3 dauer development through ligand-dependent activation by Δ7-dafachronic acid (Δ7-DA), synthesized via DAF-9 cytochrome P450.
results.evaluation: Claims C25-C32 describe the C. elegans DAF-12 pathway, all supported by appropriate citations. This provides the conceptual framework for the S. stercoralis work but represents prior knowledge from other studies.

results.result: Previous work demonstrated that pharmacologic Δ7-DA administration commits S. stercoralis larvae to reproductive development, knockout of Ss-DAF-12 prevents L3i formation, and Δ7-DA treatment reduces worm burden in a mouse hyperinfection model.
results.evaluation: Claims C33-C36 summarize prior work from the authors' group (Albarqi et al., 2016; Wang et al., 2009; Stoltzfus et al., 2014; Cheong et al., 2021; Patton et al., 2018), establishing the foundation for the current study but not representing new findings.

results.result: Δ7-DA was identified as the endogenous Ss-DAF-12 ligand through biochemical purification and UPLC-MS analysis, present at ~200 nM in FL-L3 larvae, sufficient to fully activate Ss-DAF-12.
results.evaluation: Claims C38-C41 are supported by experimental data in Figure 2. The purification strategy recovered 70% of spiked standard (Figure 2—supplement 1B), ligand activity was detected only in fraction 23 (Figure 2A), and UPLC-MS confirmed Δ7-DA identity (Figure 2B). The concentration estimate and receptor saturation claim are supported by dose-response data.

results.result: Δ7-DA levels correlate with reproductive development stages: present and abundant in FL-L1/L2, FL-L3, L3+, and parasitic adults; undetectable in FL-adults, PFL-L1, L3i, and intestinal L1-L3a larvae.
results.evaluation: Claims C42-C46 are supported by UPLC-MS quantification data in Figure 3A-C. The stage-specific pattern is clear and statistically significant (p-values provided). This establishes the correlation between Δ7-DA presence and developmental fate.

results.result: Parasitic adults have the highest Δ7-DA concentration and live up to a year in the host, while FL adults have undetectable Δ7-DA and survive only days in soil, suggesting Δ7-DA may extend parasitic adult lifespan.
results.evaluation: Claim C47 (lifespan differences) is supported by citations (Lok, 2007; Viney and Lok, 2015), and C46 shows Δ7-DA differences. However, C49 is speculative, inferring from C. elegans data (C48) without direct experimental evidence in S. stercoralis. The correlation is suggestive but causation is not demonstrated.

results.result: S. stercoralis synthesizes Δ7-DA de novo from dietary cholesterol via a biosynthetic pathway involving Ss-DAF-36, Ss-SCDH-16, and Ss-CYP22a9 (the DAF-9 ortholog), identified through functional screening of 26 CYPs.
results.evaluation: Claims C50-C51 are supported by bioinformatic analysis (Stoltzfus et al., 2012). C52 is demonstrated by 13C-cholesterol incorporation (Figure 4B). C53-C54 show functional activity of Ss-DAF-36 and Ss-SCDH-16 (Figure 4C-F). C55 is supported by unbiased screening showing only Ss-CYP22a9 synthesizes Δ7-DA (Figure 4G). The complete pathway is well-characterized.

results.result: cGMP stimulation induces Δ7-DA synthesis and Ss-cyp22a9 expression in L3i larvae; genetic disruption of Ss-cyp22a9 abolishes Δ7-DA synthesis and impairs developmental reactivation, which is rescued by exogenous Δ7-DA.
results.evaluation: Claims C56-C58 are supported by time-course data (Figure 5) showing cGMP-induced Δ7-DA synthesis, correlation with Ss-cyp22a9 expression (Figure 5—supplement 1A), and ketoconazole inhibition. C59-C61 are supported by CRISPR knockout data (Figure 5B-D) showing impaired feeding behavior and abolished Δ7-DA synthesis, with complete rescue by exogenous Δ7-DA. The genetic evidence is compelling.

results.result: In gerbils with uncomplicated S. stercoralis infection, Δ7-DA treatment for 14 days reduced fecal larval output by ~90% without significantly affecting parasitic adult numbers.
results.evaluation: Claims C62-C63 are supported by experimental data in Figure 6. The reduction in fecal larvae is statistically significant (q < 0.03), while adult parasite numbers show no significant change. The interpretation that Δ7-DA targets intestinal larval stages is consistent with the data.

results.result: In hyperinfected gerbils, Δ7-DA treatment starting at day 10 post-infection achieved 70% survival (vs. 0% for vehicle), substantially reduced intestinal parasites and L3+ larvae (90% reduction), and decreased adult parasites by 50%.
results.evaluation: Claims C64-C68 are supported by survival data (Figure 7A) and parasite burden quantification (Figure 7B-D). The survival improvement is statistically significant (q-values provided), and the differential effects on larval vs. adult stages are clearly demonstrated. The explanation for adult parasite reduction in hyperinfection vs. uncomplicated infection is logical.

results.result: Ivermectin treatment (300 μg/kg i.p.) in hyperinfected gerbils achieved ~25% survival, was as effective as Δ7-DA at removing adult parasites, but was ineffective at reducing intestinal or L3+ larval populations.
results.evaluation: Claims C69-C71 are supported by experimental data in Figure 7A-D and Figure 7—supplement 1. The survival rate, adult parasite reduction, and lack of effect on larval stages are clearly demonstrated. This establishes the complementary mechanisms of the two drugs.

results.result: Combination treatment with Δ7-DA and ivermectin achieved >75% survival in hyperinfected gerbils, reduced parasite burden at all life stages, and completely eliminated parasites in all surviving animals (vs. ≤10% parasite-free with monotherapy).
results.evaluation: Claims C72-C75 are supported by experimental data in Figure 7A-E. The synergistic effect on survival is statistically significant compared to either agent alone (q-values provided). The complete parasite elimination in all combination-treated survivors (Figure 7E) is a striking finding demonstrating potential curative efficacy.

results.result: The synergistic effect of Δ7-DA and ivermectin is explained by their complementary mechanisms: ivermectin kills adults and feeding larvae but not quiescent L3a, while Δ7-DA interferes with L3a development by inappropriately activating DAF-12.
results.evaluation: Claim C76 is supported by citation (Buonfrate et al., 2013). C77 is supported by citation (Repetto et al., 2018) and mechanistic reasoning. C78 is an inference from the experimental data showing Δ7-DA specifically targets larval stages. The mechanistic explanation is consistent with all experimental observations and provides a logical framework for the synergy.

results.result: Despite divergence in the Ss-DAF-12 ligand binding pocket (42% sequence identity with Ce-DAF-12) and unique pathway components (Ss-CYP22a9, Ss-DIP-1), Δ7-DA is conserved as the endogenous ligand.
results.evaluation: Claims C79-C81 are supported by citation (Wang et al., 2009). C82 is stated as knowledge from the current study. C83 is supported by citation (Cheong et al., 2021). This addresses the unexpected finding that Δ7-DA is conserved despite pathway divergence.

results.result: Multiple lines of evidence support Δ7-DA as the major/exclusive DAF-12 ligand: no other ligand activities detected, Ss-cyp22a9 knockout prevents DAF-12 activity (rescued by Δ7-DA), and Δ7-DA activates DAF-12 in other nematode species.
results.evaluation: Claim C84 is supported by the purification data (Figure 2). C85 is supported by the CRISPR data (Figure 5). C86 is supported by multiple citations. Together, these provide strong evidence that Δ7-DA is the relevant endogenous ligand, though the possibility of other minor ligands cannot be completely excluded.

results.result: DAF-12 is conserved across all surveyed nematode species and is required for reproductive development, suggesting that DAF-12 antagonists could provide broad-spectrum anthelmintic therapy.
results.evaluation: Claim C87 is supported by the experimental data showing Δ7-DA correlates with reproductive stages. C88 is supported by multiple citations. However, C89 is speculative—while the logic is sound, no experimental evidence for antagonist efficacy is provided. This represents a reasonable hypothesis for future work rather than a demonstrated result.

results.result: Inhibiting Δ7-DA synthesis represents an alternative therapeutic strategy, supported by ketoconazole blocking both Δ7-DA synthesis and L3i activation, though Δ7-DA itself has poor pharmacokinetic properties.
results.evaluation: Claim C90 is supported by citation (Albarqi et al., 2016) and current data (Figure 5). C91 is supported by citation (Patton et al., 2018). This identifies both the potential and limitations of current approaches, motivating future drug development.

results.result: Liganded DAF-12 is required for reproductive development while unliganded DAF-12 is required for infectious larvae production; Δ7-DA synthesis is necessary for reproduction while its absence is required for L3i/L3a development, making DAF-12 an on/off switch for autoinfection.
results.evaluation: Claims C94-C95 integrate current data (Figures 3, 5) with prior work (Cheong et al., 2021). C96-C97 are supported by the Ss-cyp22a9 knockout data (Figure 5) and stage-specific Δ7-DA quantification (Figure 3). C98 is a logical synthesis of these findings. The dual role of DAF-12 in different developmental contexts is well-established.

results.result: Pharmacologic activation of DAF-12 with Δ7-DA suppresses autoinfection and markedly reduces lethality in preclinical hyperinfection; combination with ivermectin results in near-cure, demonstrating therapeutic potential and identifying the biosynthetic enzyme as a drug target.
results.evaluation: Claims C99-C100 are supported by the gerbil hyperinfection data (Figure 7). C92 synthesizes the therapeutic implications. The preclinical efficacy is clearly demonstrated, though translation to human therapy would require additional development (better pharmacokinetics, optimized dosing).
